chunks: Al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Musa ibn Sadan, from Abdullah ibn Qasim al-Hadrami, from Abu Saeed al-Khorasani, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'Why is he named as the Qaim?' He said: 'Because he will rise after he dies. Indeed, he will rise with a great matter; he will rise by the command of Allah, the Glorified.'
ai.seo_question: Why is the Mahdi called Al-Qaim and what does his rising signify?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Kitab al-Ghayba*, Imam al-Sadiq (a.s.) clarifies that the title 'Al-Qaim' signifies not merely a political uprising, but a spiritual and cosmic resurrection following the Imam's death, executed by divine command. This highlights the Shia belief in the Imam's hidden presence and his eventual emergence to establish justice, a concept deeply rooted in the eschatological expectations of the Twelver tradition. The explanation underscores the continuity of divine authority, linking the Mahdi's role directly to the execution of Allah's will on earth.

en.sayyid-athar-husain-s-h-rizvi: H 403 - It is narrated from Fadhl bin Shazan from Musa bin Sadan from Abdullah bin Qasim Hadhrami from Abi Saeed Khurasani that he said:

I asked Imam Ja’far Sadiq (a.s), “Why is he named as Qaim?” He said: “Because he will rise after his name dies. He will establish a mighty enterprise. He will rise up by the command of Allah, the Glorified.”
